target_customer: Consumers and creators making and sharing short looped videos; advertisers
problem: People wanted to remix existing video and music into short looping clips with sound, which Vine and GIFs did not allow.

founders.name: Igor Gladkoborodov
previous_startups: Serial entrepreneurs who sold several Russian media companies (per one outlet, unnamed)

founders.name: Anton Gladkoborodov
founders.background_notes: Wikipedia also lists Mikhail Tabunov as a founder.

investors: Vaizra Investments (fund headed by VK.com founders)

competitors.name: Vine
competitors.what: Six second filmed looping videos; Twitter announced it would stop updating it in late 2016

competitors.name: Giphy
competitors.what: GIF search and sharing service moving to fill the Vine gap

technical_complexity.rationale: Video looping with soundtrack in browser and mobile is standard engineering, though serving high volume video is costly.

defensibility.rationale: Remix culture and a community gave some pull but the format was easy to copy and platforms like Vine and Giphy were larger.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Vine closed; Coub did not build a durable business on the gap and was sold to Komitet in January 2020.

market_need_then: In 2016 Twitter announced Vine would wind down and press promoted Coub as a stopgap; the site claimed 51M monthly unique visitors on its YC page.

branding.name_origin: Wikipedia and TechCrunch say the name plays on Cobb, Leonardo DiCaprio's character in Inception, with a U added because the Cobb domain was taken.
branding.domain_note: Founders added a U to Cobb because the Cobb domain was taken; operates on coub.com

identity.visual_style: Looping video grid with communities such as music, gaming, anime and memes

branding.brand_signature: The word coub as a noun for a looped clip, tied to remix culture
branding.community_and_virality: Large meme and music remix community, coverage by TechCrunch, CBS and Daily Dot as Vine alternative

brand_strength.rationale: Coub became a recognizable noun in Russian internet culture and drew international press, but it never matched Vine or Giphy reach.

outcome_analysis: Coub raised about $3.6M in total and grew an audience on remix culture and the 2016 Vine shutdown. Komitet bought it in January 2020, announced in March 2022 that it would close on April 1, then reversed and said a new team would run it, after failing to find a buyer. The site was still live in November 2026. The specific cause behind the inactive label is not stated in sources I found, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: YC status is Inactive but the website is live (copyright line to 2026 and recent posts); exit type is acquisition (Komitet, 2020) rather than shutdown, and the 2022 closure was announced then reversed. Funding totals differ by aggregator ($3.5M to $3.8M). The 2013 and 2014 rounds are labeled seed because early rounds were called Series A by some outlets. The $120K YC amount comes from vc.ru and is not YC confirmed. Competitor source date is approximate.
